RESEARCH & DIRECTIONS

Research.

How can the wave-function structure of noninteracting electrons shape correlated physics?

01 / ESTABLISHED RESEARCH

Quantum Geometry

Can the quantum geometry of noninteracting bands guide our understanding of correlated matter?

Quantum geometry encodes how Bloch wave functions vary with momentum. For time-reversal-breaking Chern bands, Kähler geometry provides a framework for understanding ideal band geometry and its connection to fractional Chern insulators. Our work generalizes this geometric language to time-reversal-symmetric Kramers pairs: quaternion-Kähler structures and non-Abelian metric–curvature relations offer a starting point for asking analogous questions in systems that preserve time reversal.

This framework provides a starting point for identifying geometric conditions relevant to time-reversal-symmetric correlated phases.

02 / ESTABLISHED RESEARCH

Band Topology

What topological information is lost when we look only at the occupied bands?

Some band-topological structures depend on the wave functions of both occupied and unoccupied states. In the real Hopf insulator, we characterized delicate three-dimensional topology in four-band systems with spinless PT symmetry, including independent Hopf invariants and associated boundary phenomena. I am also interested in the structure of unconventional topological phase transitions.

These results highlight why the full multiband wave-function structure matters for topological classification.

03 / BROADER RESEARCH INTERESTS

Correlated Quantum Matter

How do the traces of noninteracting band structure shape what emerges from electron correlations?

My broader interests include correlations in electronic bands, topological order, symmetry-protected topological phases, and generalized symmetries. I hope to investigate how multiband quantum geometry can constrain or guide the emergence of time-reversal-symmetric correlated phases.

A future direction is to connect single-particle geometric constraints with concrete many-body models and observables.
